I am 64 years old and have farmed these same fields in Quzhou County since I was a young man. I only finished primary school, but I know this land better than any book-learned expert. It is early spring now, and my winter wheat is already in the ground — I sowed it last October after the National Day holiday, as my father taught me. I have 8 mu of flat, good-quality land, and I will stick to the wheat-maize double-cropping system. It is the only rotation I trust, and the grain station buys both crops reliably. 

For the winter wheat, I will apply top-dressing nitrogen when the wheat turns green, irrigate three times total (green-up, jointing, and heading), and spray pesticides twice if I see aphids or rust. I use an improved wheat seed variety because the county seed station recommends it and it resists lodging. For the summer maize, I will plant hybrid seed immediately after wheat harvest in early June — every day delayed costs yield. I will give the maize two irrigations and two pesticide sprays. I am getting older and my back hurts, so for the maize I will sow directly into the wheat stubble with no-tillage to save time and diesel. I use plenty of fertilizer because I have learned over decades that cutting back means lower yields, and I need the grain to support myself and my wife.
